transformations: Preserve original FBX bytes; validate and share matching duplicate skin bind poses at runtime.
Use prefab material assignments instead of stale embedded FBX texture links.
Downsample selected base colors to a maximum 1024 pixels; use JPEG quality 90 for opaque maps.
Retarget the approved CC0 run; use project-authored reference-stance idle instead of the borrowed short-period idle. Unity .anim controllers are not executed.
Rebuild a coherent canonical bone parent chain while preserving every bind matrix, then share it across the 14 parts.
Calibrate auxiliary reference poses and hip/leg scale; bake shoe-sole nonpenetration offline.
Mask borrowed arm/finger tracks; apply a native static rifle pose, analytic elbow hints, right-hand attachment and weapon-relative left wrist target.
Keep the procedural rest muzzle at (0.13, 1.39, -0.871); native simulation-owned carry transforms move both displayed and authoritative muzzle together without renderer readback.
Restore Repeat wrapping for the eye texture: the actual eye UVs occupy U=1.0017..1.9998 and include negative V coordinates.
Attach the supplied M1935 helmet to the canonical Head bone using the actual prefab transforms, original FBX and base-color bytes.
limitations: Candidate historical appearance; exact Taierzhuang unit issue not verified.
Static rifle hold and finger curl are project-authored poses, not a complete military animation library.
No authored aim-transition, reload-hand, crouch or death clips; analytic hand alignment is interim, not final animation quality.
FBXLoader emits five more-than-four-skinning-weight warnings and drops excess influences; affected vertex count has not been enumerated. No lossless-import claim.
Existing collision and hit proxy retained; not bone-accurate damage zones.
The selected KayKit walking clip remains adapted from a stylized source; final military movement quality is unverified.

appearance.basis: Project-authored runtime derivatives of the permission-recorded source character; no additional face downloads.
appearance.traits: 8 mild jaw/cheek/nose/brow geometry families, 5 face-and-hand complexion tints, 3 mild torso volume variants.
appearance.ownership: Deterministic per original unit/soldier identity; restored on pooled view rebind. Shared source geometry is not mutated.
appearance.limits: Original base mesh, face texture and hairstyle remain shared. Distant LOD retains complexion/approximate build but simplifies facial geometry. Not 100 independently scanned faces.

evaluation.evidence: Initial integration before motion feedback: normal 100v100 Y control and resources preserved; original soldier-192 AI shot recorded at simulation time 55.5293.
evaluation.notApproved: Final historical accuracy, full military animation quality, full skinned-army performance and user quality acceptance remain unverified.
evaluation.feedbackRevision: Native idle and distance-driven run/carry verified in normal 100v100 movement observation: hips steady while idle, gun moves with body, action reset only on bind, muzzle alignment remains within 0.0001m.
evaluation.feedbackCombat: Two new full-battle observations did not capture this soldier firing (one never engaged; one was killed). Existing explicit 5v5 functional diagnostic recorded actual native soldier-7 AI fire at t=2.548 with the moving authoritative muzzle. This is not a new full-scale AI/performance pass.
evaluation.scope: All friendly ground soldiers share uniform and helmet; only nearest bounded pool uses full skeletons, distant soldiers use shared baked pose instances. This is not a full-asset performance pass.
evaluation.uniformRendering: All friendly ground identities receive this appearance at creation, including reinforcements. Up to 6 high-quality or 3 low-quality independent rigs; farther agents use 13 shared standing/walking/running pose banks with a single padded 2560px atlas material. No actor is deleted to satisfy rendering limits.
evaluation.walking: Official KayKit 1.1 Walking_C GLB retained full rotation curves; A/B judged too exaggerated. Remains stylized and subject to user review.
